new_statements.quote: Although tonal contrast is found in virtually all of the the Lakes Plain languages, it will not be shown in the word list transcriptions. Additionally, stress is not marked because only a few original word lists marked it and it has not been found to be contrastive in any of the Lakes Plain languages to date. [p.160] ... Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages and therefore was most likely a feature of some of the protolanguages as well. ... All the modern languages have at least high and low tone. [p.152]

new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional rule exists. The only published prosodic statement covering Saponi is a family-level generalization by the Lakes Plain comparativist: all Lakes Plain languages are tonal (at least H and L), and stress has not been found contrastive in any of them. For Saponi itself the only data are a 1986 SIL survey word list (Bouwman and Holster, Botawa) reproduced without stress or tone marks; Clouse never examined Saponi and states that for the Far West group only word lists exist.
new_statements.exceptions: The tone claim is hedged ('virtually all'); no Saponi tone data are cited anywhere, and Wikipedia (unsourced) questions Saponi's Lakes Plain membership on pronominal grounds, so the family-level claim's applicability to Saponi is untested.
new_statements.domain_note: Survey word list (citation forms); family-level statement about word lists across the family, not a Saponi description.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Saponi [sapo1254, ISO spi] of Botawa village, Waropen Bawah subdistrict; extinct (Ethnologue: no known L1 speakers, 'moribund 2000 S. Wurm'; Clouse & Clouse 1993 gave population 10). Glottolog places it under Lakes Plain > Far West Lakes Plain > Rasawa-Saponi (Clouse 1997's 'Rasawa-Saponi Family'); Wikipedia (unsourced, apparently following Usher) treats it as unclassified, lexically Lakes Plain but pronominally East Bird's Head-like. The only Saponi data are the 1986 Bouwman-Holster survey list as reprinted in Clouse 1997 App. 3.
